narrative.overview:
The site is a technical drawing sheet: a cream plate divided by hairline rules into cells, each cell holding one CSS feature with its live demo as the drawing. Nothing floats. Cards, filters, header, ticker, results bar and reading pages are all regions of the same ruled plate, separated by 1px warm rules that collapse between neighbours rather than by gaps and shadows.

The frame is deliberately quiet so the demos lead. One forest green carries every piece of state and action: the wordmark disc, the Production ready tag, selected filters, primary actions, links, the focus ring and the ticker separators. Everything else is ink on cream. Type splits into two voices: a heavy, slightly condensed, uppercase Archivo for names (wordmark, card titles, page headings) and Geist Mono uppercase for every label, tag, control, count and the ticker. Running prose stays in sentence-case Archivo at regular weight.

The world refuses the category default of rounded floating cards on a grey canvas with pill tags. Corners are square; the only curve in the system is the solid forest disc.
keyCharacteristics: Cream sheet, near-black ink, one forest green; no other interface hue.
1px warm rules divide every region; cells share edges instead of sitting apart.
Square corners on everything except the forest disc motif.
Heavy condensed uppercase Archivo for names; mono uppercase for every label.
Readiness is shape-coded: solid forest, outlined forest, dashed ink.
Flat: no shadows for depth; the drawing paper panel is set into the sheet, not lifted.

Motion has one authored moment: filter and sort changes glide each sheet cell to its new place (View Transitions, 400ms on cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)); cells that arrive are drawn in top to bottom with a clip-path, cells that leave fade out in 150ms. Supporting motion: the code disclosure opens with ::details-content + interpolate-size (300ms in, 200ms out), the mobile drawer slides in over 300ms and out over 200ms with a fading backdrop, the ticker, and 150ms colour feedback (filter boxes, Copy turning forest when it succeeds). Reduced motion skips the cell transition and the disclosure animation and keeps colour feedback.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Forest is the only interface hue. Anything that is selected, ready, primary or a link is forest; everything else is ink, pencil or a warm neutral. Do not introduce a second accent, a warning colour or a status red.

rules.name: The Demo Blue Rule
rules.body: Demos keep their own blue accent (#2563eb), and the interface never uses it. Blue inside a demo panel is the feature; blue in the frame would compete with it.

rules.name: The Ink Edge Rule
rules.body: A standalone control (button, input, select, disclosure) has a sheet-ink edge or a forest fill. Warm rules divide cells and frame passive chips; they never carry an interactive edge alone.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Names are heavy condensed uppercase Archivo; labels are mono uppercase. Prose is the only sentence-case text. A new element picks one of the three; it never mixes a third style in.

rules.name: The Ramp Is Closed Rule
rules.body: The sizes above are the full ramp. A new surface reuses one of them rather than adding an in-between size.

rules.name: The Set-In Rule
rules.body: Panels are set into the sheet with a 1px rule, never lifted off it. No drop shadows, no hover lift, no glow.

rules.name: The Only Curve Rule
rules.body: Nothing is rounded except the forest disc. A disc is always solid forest and decorative; it is never a button, avatar or badge.

rules.name: The Dashed Means Partial Rule
rules.body: A dashed edge means "not fully there": Experimental readiness and partial browser support. Do not use dashes decoratively.

dos: Do divide regions with 1px warm rules (border) and let neighbouring cells share one rule.
Do keep every corner square; reserve the circle for the solid forest disc.
Do use forest for every selected, ready, primary or link state, and nothing else.
Do code readiness by shape as well as colour: solid forest, outlined forest, dashed ink.
Do set names in heavy condensed uppercase Archivo (800, wdth 88, -0.02em) and every label in Geist Mono uppercase at 0.8125rem with 0.04em tracking.
Do give every standalone control an ink edge or a forest fill and a 44px minimum target.
Do put demos on drawing paper (paper) inside a ruled panel, and let them keep their own blue.
donts: Don't use rounded cards, pill tags or floating cards on a grey canvas.
Don't add drop shadows, hover lift or glow; panels are set in, not raised.
Don't use the demo blue (#2563eb) anywhere in the interface frame.
Don't introduce a second interface hue, including green/amber/red status colours.
Don't use dashed edges except for Experimental readiness and partial browser support.
Don't add type sizes outside the documented ramp.
Don't animate anything beyond the ticker, 150ms colour transitions and the drawer slide.
